quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025) consolidated results: revenue JPY 2,534,203 million (98.4% of the prior year), operating profit JPY 126,373 million (prior year JPY 181,515 million), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 16,109 million (prior year JPY 108,069 million). Management states revenue fell, despite higher motorcycle unit sales in Indonesia, the Philippines and Thailand, because of a production and shipment halt in Vietnam and lower unit sales of water vehicles and outdoor land vehicles; operating profit fell on US tariffs, higher procurement costs, higher SG&A including R&D and labour costs, and an impairment of Outdoor Land Vehicle property, plant and equipment; net profit also fell on a reversal of deferred tax assets. Segment revenue / segment profit: Land Mobility JPY 1,615,138 million / JPY 108,693 million; Marine JPY 527,630 million / JPY 53,593 million; Outdoor Land Vehicle JPY 148,526 million / loss JPY 39,757 million; Robotics JPY 111,478 million / loss JPY 565 million; Financial Services JPY 114,033 million / JPY 21,056 million. Motorcycle unit sales 4,999,132 (100.8% of the prior year); the company produces mainly to forecast (build-to-stock).
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 2,534,203 million (98.4% of prior year); operating profit JPY 126,373 million; profit attributable to owners JPY 16,109 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Robotics segment (surface mounters, semiconductor back-end manufacturing equipment, industrial robots, industrial unmanned helicopters), FY2025: revenue JPY 111,478 million (98.4% of the prior year), segment loss JPY 565 million (prior year loss JPY 3,003 million). Management states sales of semiconductor back-end manufacturing equipment increased as demand for generative AI and advanced packaging grew, while surface mounter and industrial robot unit sales fell below the prior year, leaving segment revenue flat; the loss narrowed on lower manufacturing costs and an improved marginal profit ratio. Production of surface mounters and industrial robots: 29,166 units (87.5% of the prior year). Robotics capital expenditure in the segment note JPY 7,811 million. From January 1, 2026 the industrial unmanned aircraft business moved from Robotics to Other; on the new segmentation FY2025 Robotics segment profit was JPY 1,664 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Robotics revenue JPY 111,478 million (98.4%); segment loss JPY 565 million (prior year loss JPY 3,003 million); restated segment profit JPY 1,664 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Investment: FY2025 capital expenditure totalled JPY 128.0 billion (Land Mobility JPY 73.7 billion; Marine JPY 40.1 billion, including outboard motor capacity expansion; Outdoor Land Vehicle JPY 2.5 billion, including golf car capacity expansion; Robotics JPY 7.7 billion, mainly R&D for surface mounters and industrial robots). Group R&D spending was JPY 159.1 billion, of which Robotics JPY 12.3 billion. Plan for 2026: capital expenditure JPY 140,000 million (Land Mobility JPY 87,900 million, Marine JPY 30,800 million, Outdoor Land Vehicle JPY 9,700 million, Robotics JPY 8,500 million, Financial Services JPY 800 million, Other JPY 2,300 million; mainly production and R&D facilities) and R&D spending of JPY 170.0 billion. No material facility disposals are planned apart from routine replacement.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 capex JPY 128.0 billion; R&D JPY 159.1 billion; 2026 plan capex JPY 140,000 million (Robotics JPY 8,500 million), R&D JPY 170.0 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Medium-term management plan (from 2025): portfolio of core businesses (motorcycles, Marine), strategic businesses (Robotics, SPV electrically power-assisted bicycles, Outdoor Land Vehicle) and new businesses; financial targets ROE around 14%, ROIC around 8% and ROA around 9% (each a three-year average), and over the long term every business above ROIC 12.5%. For Robotics the company aims, through the 2025 integration that formed Yamaha Robotics Co., Ltd., to become one of the world's top-class total solution companies in semiconductor back-end processes and electronic component mounting. In SPV it acquired the bicycle drive unit (e-Kit) subsidiary of German auto-parts maker Brose in 2025, establishing Yamaha Motor eBike Systems GmbH in Germany; FY2025 results include its August-December 2025 results.
quarterly_data.figure: ROE around 14%; ROIC around 8%; ROA around 9% (three-year averages); ROIC 12.5% long-term hurdle for every business

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D results in Robotics, FY2025: in semiconductor back-end manufacturing equipment, the company carried out a NEDO-funded project, 'development of chip-on-wafer direct bonding 3D stacking integration technology for post-5G', jointly with the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST) and Tokyo University of Science; it also developed the entry-level solder paste printer YRP10e (surface mounters) and the 7-axis collaborative robot 'Yamaha Motor Cobot' (industrial robots).

quarterly_data.quarter: Yamaha Motor annual securities report: FY2025 (03-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management states the business environment in the US, its main market, has changed significantly because of tariffs and other factors, but demand for large outboard motors is expected to keep growing steadily, and it is continuing development to expand its large outboard line-up during the medium-term plan; it expects the market for Outdoor Land Vehicle products to expand over the long term and will rebuild that business's earnings base through cost control and resource reallocation in light of US tariffs and changing demand.
